transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Redwood CSM); Evan Patel (DataWave - Platform Lead), Sofia Ramos (DataWave - SecOps), Marcus Lee (DataWave - ML Eng), Hannah Cho (DataWave - Network)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot. Reviewed last week's benchmark results, networking/peering status, runtime upgrade plan, and tuning changes (prefix cache, batch window). Identified remaining blockers for on-prem upgrade and a set of follow-ups: updated network diagram, firewall rules, apply prefix caching and re-run benchmarks, schedule upgrade maintenance window.

Topics:
- Benchmarks: latency, throughput, tail spikes
- Networking: VPC peering, NAT, firewall rules, BGP/Transit GW considerations
- Runtime upgrade: v1.8.2 -> v1.9.0 (kernel selection, quantization support)
- Tuning: prefix/KV caching, batch window, autoscaler min replicas
- Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2 notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: ok good morning everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly sync for the private vpc pilot. um Maya and I will run through the results then we can get status on networking and the upgrade window.
[00:18] Evan: morning, thanks. we got the last run results yesterday, I'll hand over to Marcus to summarize.
[00:24] Marcus: yep, so the benchmark we ran against the pilot cluster (model pinned to redwood-gpt-small-int8) showed median generation latency ~85ms, p50 around 80ms, p95 ~240ms, p99 ~420ms. throughput peaked at about 90 requests/sec with our test payloads (avg tokens ~60). there were periodic tail spikes that seem correlated with cold KV cache events and occasional autoscaler spin-up.
[00:46] Maya: okay that's consistent with what we saw in the hosted runs. the tail latency jump usually matches when a new instance is created and the KV cache isn't warmed. did you run any runs with prefix-caching on?
[00:58] Marcus: we did a small run with it off and then a short test with prefix caching enabled — saw p95 drop to ~160ms and p99 to ~300ms, throughput was about the same, so cache helps. but we didn't tune the batch window.
[01:16] Jesse: cool, so two actionable things: enable prefix caching consistently for the next benchmark and adjust batch window to 8-12ms to allow slightly larger microbatches without hurting latency. Maya can share a recommended config.
[01:29] Maya: yeah I'll add that in the config. also recommend minimum replicas be set to 2 on the pilot so you avoid cold starts during short spikes. autoscaler policy can keep cost reasonable with scale-down delay.
[01:40] Sofia: quick question on security — we're verifying that logs and payloads never leave our VPC. is the control plane fully private for the private offering, or is there still any egress to redwood-hosted services?
[01:52] Jesse: good question. for the private deployment the control plane talks over a secure channel to the customer-managed control plane endpoint; we support private endpoints and can do no-egress where the control plane is in your environment. for the hosted-managed control plane there's some telemetry flow but it's opt-in. we'll send the security diagram.
[02:06] Tom: to add, we have a hardened on-prem option where the control plane is customer-hosted and logs are stored in your S3/gcs equivalent and KMS/HSM integrations are available.
[02:18] Hannah: network status from our side: VPC peering with Redwood dev test account completed, but we hit an issue with route tables — the peer-route wasn't propagated to our private subnet that hosts the pilot cluster. we suspect it's a broadcasting route propagation setting on the Transit GW.
[02:34] Maya: that matches a misconfig we saw before. typical fixes: ensure the TGW route table has the proper attachments and add explicit route entries for the subnets. also ensure the security groups allow the control plane IPs and the Redood-- I mean Redwood agent IPs. sometimes the agent name gets transcribed wrong, sorry.
[02:51] (laughter)
[02:55] Hannah: yeah we saw some packets get dropped. we can share traceroutes.
[02:58] Jesse: please send the traceroute and we'll have network to network folks look. also Maya will share the exact IP ranges and firewall ports needed (443/5671 for control plane and 10250-ish for kubelet if on-prem).
[03:12] Evan: regarding the runtime upgrade, what's the risk of moving from v1.8.2 to v1.9.0? we need kernel and quantization fixes but don't want downtime.
[03:22] Maya: v1.9.0 contains kernel selection improvements for r/w attention and better int8 dequant paths. we've validated on similar hardware (A10G in your case) — the main risk is incompatibility with custom runtime hooks or modified docker images. upgrade steps: roll one node at a time with health checks, keep canary traffic on a small percentage, and snapshot the KV cache if you need fast rollback.
[03:40] Marcus: do we need any model re-quantization? we used the redwood int8 artifact.
[03:44] Maya: no model re-quant required for this patch; it's runtime-only but may change perf. we'll run canary runs post-upgrade.
[03:50] Sofia: audit and compliance — we need to ensure audit logs show model version and kit selection for each decision, and KMS key usage is logged. can you confirm?
[03:59] Tom: yes, our audit log integration records the model version, runtime version, the tenant id, and KMS key id for encryption operations. we'll include a sample event in the security pack.
[04:10] Hannah: firewall rules we need to confirm — we'll patch our perimeter on Monday and would like the exact list of IPs and ports to open.
[04:18] Jesse: Maya will send the list; I'll attach the SOW and the security diagram.
[04:23] Maya: also a note on routing: if you use AWS Transit Gateway and have on-prem over VPN to the TGW, ensure route propagation is enabled and that the TGW route table is associated with the attachment for the pilot VPC. otherwise you'll see that peer-route not propagate.
[04:39] Hannah: got it, that explains the symptom. will check with infra.
[04:42] Evan: on benchmarks — what test harness should we use to reproduce your numbers? we used the internal runner but want to be sure.
[04:49] Maya: use the redwood-loadbench script we shared last month (link in the deck). key flags: concurrency, tokens per request, and enable-prefix-cache boolean. we'll include the wrapper command. also recommend running with warm-up for 5 minutes to stabilize KV cache.
[05:03] Marcus: noted. will also try increasing batch window to 12ms.
[05:06] Jesse: any blockers on the legal/compliance sign-off?
[05:09] Sofia: signed off on DPA but need one more review for the additional data residency appendix. legal will come back by end of next week.
[05:16] Tom: adding that Redwood can provide SOC2 artifacts and ISO attestation we used for similar customers; will attach.
[05:22] Jesse: great. wrapping up — recap of actions: Maya sends tuned config and firewall IPs; Jesse shares SOW and pricing; Hannah validates routing and confirms firewall change; Evan/Marcus run the benchmark with prefix caching, warm-up, and new batch window and share results.
[05:37] Evan: sounds good, thanks all.
[05:39] Jesse: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and update the pilot board.
